points_harris_binomial — 2D edges op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "points_harris_binomial", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: points_harris_binomial (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*The output is shown in a viridis-like pseudo-colour (dark purple = low, yellow = high) so that a field of quantities — distance, phase, orientation, depth — can be read.*

▸ points_harris_binomial: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Harris corner response preceded by binomial (Gaussian) smoothing. First smooths the image with a sigma determined by `b, then computes the Harris response on top of it (using corner_harris if skimage is available, otherwise manually computing the structure tensor, with k=0.04). Corresponds to HALCON's points_harris_binomial` (Detect points of interest using the binomial approximation of the Harris operator.).

> The detailed description below is the original text — the summary and the headings are translated.

`a が Harris 応答自体のシグマ(0.5〜2.5)を、b` が前段の平滑化シグマ

(0.5〜2.0)を振る。両方が使われる。
